title: Breaking the Alphabet: Rethinking File Ordering in Code Review
abstract: arXiv:2609.04207v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Effective code review is central to maintaining software quality, yet there is limited research about how the ordering of changed files in Pull Requests (PRs) influences review effectiveness. Most popular code review tools default to alphabetical ordering, favoring predictability over contextual relevance. While prior studies examined how file position shapes reviewer attention, it remains unclear how such ordering influences cognitive load and perceived review thoroughness. This study presents the first large-scale survey of 1,355 professional developers across 182 widely used open-source projects to investigate how file ordering impacts review behavior, comprehension, and perceived effectiveness. Our mixed-methods analysis reveals that only 10.2% of reviewers consider alphabetical ordering optimal, underscoring a cognitive misalignment in their interpretation of code changes. translated_title: 打破字母顺序：重新思考代码审查中的文件排序
translated_abstract: 有效的代码审查对于维护软件质量至关重要，然而关于拉取请求（PR）中变更文件的排序如何影响审查效果的研究却很有限。大多数流行的代码审查工具默认采用字母顺序排序，更看重可预测性而非上下文相关性。尽管先前的研究考察了文件位置如何影响审查者的注意力，但这种排序如何影响认知负荷和感知到的审查彻底性仍不清楚。本研究首次对来自182个广泛使用的开源项目的1,355名专业开发者进行了大规模调查，以探究文件排序如何影响审查行为、理解能力以及感知效果。我们的混合方法分析显示，仅有10.2%的审查者认为字母顺序排序是最优的，这凸显了他们在解读代码变更时的认知错位。尽管一些开发者欣赏其可预测性，但更多（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 通过对182个开源项目1355名开发者的首次大规模调查发现，仅10.2%的审查者认为代码审查中文件按字母顺序排序是最优的，揭示了默认字母排序与开发者认知之间的错位，表明需要重新思考PR中的文件排序方式。
en_tdlr: A first large-scale survey of 1,355 developers across 182 open-source projects reveals that only 10.2% of reviewers consider alphabetical file ordering optimal in code review, exposing a cognitive misalignment and calling for rethinking file ordering in Pull Requests.
